newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa sees more preferred cargo agents.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees more preferred cargo agents.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG will seek closer partnership with selected freight forwarders in future, Michael Kraus, the cargo airline's business development and global accounts manager, said.
"Forwarders will be sales partners or logistics partners. We will define which types of partnership and what type of commodity the partner supplies," he told a news conference on Thursday.
"There will be more preferred agent agreements and we must look at yields. Those (agents) who contribute more financially are worth more," he said.
The airline already offers lower air cargo rates to its A-grade agents than to its B-grade agents.
Kraus said Lufthansa Cargo earned 95 per cent of sales revenue through forwarders at present.
Large forwarders had the advantage of being able to offer global logistics services and networks while smaller agents often had close client contact, he noted.

Asked by Reuters whether forwarders could in time face similar market conditions to travel agencies, Kraus said: "I cannot imagine that with forwarders there will be any different development to the travel agents' industry."
German travel agents currently face the prospect of re-structured and lower Lufthansa commission payments and are seeing large chains gain increasing dominance of the market.
Kraus said added-value partnerships combining know-how, resources and improved transport connections could offer clients better services than integrators and provide global door-to-door services.
"We are not copying integrators. If we get partnerships going then we are not afraid of integrators," he said.
But he noted integrators have changed the nature of the air cargo market after the traditional cargo community first decided they were not part of their market.
Kraus cited the creation together with Schenker International of a logistics chain for the Siemens semi-conductor plant in Dresden as one successful partnership.

Another was the textile industry distribution with forwarder Deutsche Kleiderspedition (DKS) of hanging garments made in China, collected in Hong Kong and flown to Frankfurt for distribution. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
